intro: Copperline sells home goods online and runs on a billing system older than most of its engineers. You are its first Claude architect. Its teams are waiting for you, each with a system to build on Claude, and each will bring you its decisions and its incidents.

chapters.title: Know the Legacy
chapters.intro: The platform team wants an agent that helps engineers explore the legacy billing code, generate boilerplate and automate chores, using the built-in tools and MCP servers. Nobody fully understands that code any more. Start here.
chapters.outro: Engineers now ask the agent before they ask each other, and the billing code has a map.

chapters.title: The Front Desk
chapters.intro: The support team wants an agent that resolves returns, billing disputes and account issues on first contact, using get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund and escalate_to_human, and that hands over to a person when it should. The target is 80% resolved at first contact.
chapters.outro: The agent closes most cases alone, and the people behind it get cases they can act on.

chapters.title: Guard the Pipeline
chapters.intro: The delivery team wants Claude Code in CI/CD: reviewing pull requests, generating tests and commenting where it matters, without burying developers in false positives.
chapters.outro: Reviews arrive before the coffee does, and developers read them.

chapters.title: The Research Desk
chapters.intro: The strategy team wants a research system: a coordinator that delegates to subagents for web search, document analysis, synthesis and report writing, and produces reports whose every claim has a source.
chapters.outro: Leadership reads the reports and, more to the point, trusts the citations.
